about: The consecration of the chalice. Its words combine expressions from the institution narratives in Matthew 26, Mark 14, Luke 22 and 1 Corinthians 11. “Mystérium fídei” does not occur in those accounts, while “ætérni” corresponds to Hebrews 13:20. The concluding command draws on Luke 22:19 and 1 Corinthians 11:25–26.

s02.translation: In a similar way, when supper was ended,

s03.narrative: The priest takes the chalice in both hands.

s04.translation: He took this precious chalice in His holy and venerable hands,

s05.narrative: The priest bows his head again.

s06.translation: and once more giving You thanks,

s07.narrative: Holding the chalice in his left hand, the priest signs the cross over it with his right.

s08.translation: He said the blessing and gave the chalice to His disciples, saying:

s09.translation: Take this, all of you, and drink from it:

s10.narrative: The priest speaks the words of consecration over the chalice attentively, without break and silently, holding it slightly raised.

s11.translation: For this is the chalice of My Blood, the Blood of the new and eternal covenant: the mystery of faith: which will be poured out for you and for many for the forgiveness of sins.

s12.narrative: The words spoken, the priest sets the chalice on the corporal and says silently:

s13.translation: As often as you shall do these things, you shall do them in memory of Me.

s14.narrative: The priest genuflects and adores, rises, shows the chalice to the people, sets it down, covers it and genuflects again.

w001.function: “Símili modo” is an ablative of manner: “in a similar way”.

w004.function: An impersonal past construction: “when supper was ended”.

w006.function: A present participle referring to Christ, the subject of “benedíxit” (w021).

w009.function: The epithet with “Cálicem” (w010) — an echo of Ps 22:5: calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est.

w017.function: An adverb marking the repetition of the bow made at the consecration of the bread.

w022.function: Over the chalice there is no fregit: the breaking belonged to the bread.

w030.function: The pronoun points to the chalice. Ex eo, out of it, where the bread had ex hoc, of this.

w038.function: A genitive agreeing with “testaménti” (w041), not with “Sánguinis” (w036).

w040.function: Eternal stands in no account of the institution. The phrase blood of the eternal covenant comes from Hebrews.

w041.function: A genitive with “novi” (w038) and “ætérni” (w040), hanging on “Sánguinis” (w036): the blood of the new and eternal covenant.

w042.function: Nominative, governed by nothing: the received reading holds it in apposition to “Calix” (w035), an older tradition hears an exclamation standing on its own, and both words carry the disputed flag. These two words stand in no account of the institution.

w044.function: The masculine decides nothing here: “Calix” (w035) and “Sánguinis” (w036) are both masculine, so the form leaves the antecedent open. Mt 26:28 says it of the blood. English which leaves it open, as the Latin does.

w050.function: Future, not past: at the moment of the Supper the blood had not yet been shed.

w056.function: A future perfect: an action complete before the one “faciétis” (w060) names. The same form can be a perfect subjunctive, and the future that follows decides it.

w058.function: The genitive of the personal pronoun, not the possessive adjective: memory of Me, not My memory.
